summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked; one WebSearch used). No document retrieved; every empirical and legal item is pending. Q1: built a safeguard requirement matrix spanning Nepal's Constitution, Environment Protection Act 2076 and Rules 2077 (search located Law Commission and ECOLEX copies), Land Acquisition Act 2034, LARR Policy 2015, Forest, RTI and disability laws, ILO C169 (ratification to be confirmed from NORMLEX), UNDRIP, and WB ESF, ADB SPS/ESF, AIIB ESF and IFC PS5/PS7; no gap is asserted until texts are read. Q2: listed candidate projects and evaluators (ADB IED, WB IEG and Inspection Panel, ADB Accountability Mechanism, KfW, OAG, NHRC, Supreme Court) for a project-level displacement evidence table; no counts. Q3: a design-only, ethics-reviewed citizen-priorities survey (stratified two-stage sample on the NPHC 2021 frame, layered consent, accessibility, data protection) that cannot be piloted or fielded without recorded human approvals for fieldwork and contact_third_party under src/orchestrator/approvals.py; none exist.

findings.claim: Q1: EIA/IEE/BES screening under the Environment Protection Act 2076 and Rules 2077 - which infrastructure categories and size thresholds trigger each level, and the approving authority (federal/provincial/local).
findings.period: Law in force as of retrieval date (Act 2076 = 2019; Rules 2077 = 2020)
findings.note: Required: official texts of Act and Rules incl. schedules; thresholds read from schedules only; amendments since 2020 recorded. Leads: 14C-L01, 14C-L02, 14C-L03.

findings.claim: Q1: Public-consultation steps in the EIA process (scoping notice, public hearing, written opinions from local levels, disclosure period, language/format of notices) and whether hearings must occur at the project site.
findings.note: Required: rule numbers and verbatim procedural text; time limits recorded from the gazetted text (search-snippet figures deliberately not used). Leads: 14C-L01, 14C-L02.

findings.claim: Q1: Compulsory land acquisition - procedure, compensation basis, objection/appeal rights, treatment of tenants and non-titled occupants under the Land Acquisition Act 2034 and the 2015 LARR policy; whether replacement cost is binding or policy guidance.
findings.note: Required: current consolidated Act text, LARR policy text and any cabinet-approved guidelines; confirm legal status of each. Coordinate single observation set with 11A. Leads: 14C-L05, 14C-L06, 14C-L07, 14C-L08, 14C-L09.

findings.claim: Q1: FPIC / consultation obligations for indigenous nationalities - ILO C169 ratification status and date for Nepal, the Articles applicable to infrastructure and relocation, domestic implementing legislation (if any), and CEACR comments on implementation.
findings.period: C169 ratification date (to verify); CEACR comments by year
findings.note: Required: NORMLEX ratification record for Nepal; C169 text; CEACR comments on Nepal; UNDRIP text and Nepal vote; check for a domestic FPIC procedure. Brief states Nepal ratified C169; this is to be confirmed from NORMLEX, not assumed. Leads: 14C-L17, 14C-L18, 14C-L19, 14C-L20, 14C-L21, 14C-L15.

findings.claim: Q1: Constitutional rights engaged by displacement and consultation (property and compensation, information, clean environment, indigenous/Dalit/women/disability rights, natural-resource benefit sharing).
findings.note: Required: article numbers and verbatim text from the authoritative Nepali text with MoLJPA translation. Leads: 14C-L09, 14C-L10.

findings.claim: Q1: Other domestic laws affecting project consultation: Forest Act 2076 forest-land diversion conditions; Right to Information Act 2064 disclosure; Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2074 accessibility.
findings.period: Laws in force as of retrieval
findings.note: Required: official texts; exact URLs to locate on lawcommission.gov.np. Leads: 14C-L11, 14C-L16, 14C-L14.

findings.claim: Q1: MDB safeguard requirements for Nepal projects: World Bank ESF (ESS1, ESS5, ESS7, ESS10) and legacy OP 4.12/4.10; ADB SPS 2009 and successor ESF; AIIB ESF; IFC Performance Standards 5 and 7 - trigger conditions for FPIC/consent vs consultation, entitlements for non-titled occupants, livelihood restoration, grievance mechanisms.
findings.period: Framework versions and effective dates to record
findings.note: Required: framework texts with effective dates and transition rules; gap analysis vs Nepali law (see specific.safeguard_requirements.gap_matrix). Leads: 14C-L22, 14C-L23, 14C-L24, 14C-L25, 14C-L26.

findings.claim: Q2: Documented resettlement outcomes for major Nepal infrastructure projects (hydropower, roads, transmission, water supply, airports): households/persons physically and economically displaced, compensation and resettlement cost, time to payment, livelihood restoration and post-project income relative to baseline.
findings.period: Project-specific; evaluation years to record (calendar) and project FYs
findings.note: Required: evaluation/completion reports and monitoring reports for each project in specific.displacement_evidence.candidate_projects; record counts as published with definitions (physical vs economic displacement; titled vs non-titled). Leads: 14C-L27, 14C-L28, 14C-L29, 14C-L30, 14C-L31, 14C-L32, 14C-L33, 14C-L39.

findings.claim: Q2: Grievances, accountability-mechanism complaints and court cases related to displacement/consultation on Nepal projects (count by mechanism and outcome).
findings.note: Required: case registers of Inspection Panel and ADB AM filtered for Nepal; NHRC reports; Supreme Court decisions. Count only after retrieval. Leads: 14C-L27, 14C-L28, 14C-L35, 14C-L36.

findings.claim: Q2: Land acquisition and compensation as a cause of project delay/cost overrun in Nepal public investment.
findings.note: Required: OAG and NPC project-level delay causes; WB bottlenecks analysis section on land. Shared evidence with 06C. Leads: 14C-L37, 14C-L39, 14C-L40.

findings.claim: Q2: International comparator evidence on long-run resettlement livelihood outcomes (e.g. Nam Theun 2 monitoring; MDB portfolio reviews).
findings.note: Required: panel-of-experts/IEG reports; used only as comparator, not Nepal evidence. Leads: 14C-L32, 14C-L34.

findings.claim: Q3: A citizen-priorities survey is designed but NOT fielded. Fielding, piloting, recruiting enumerators, contacting any person or organisation, or publishing the instrument requires recorded approvals under src/orchestrator/approvals.py for actions 'fieldwork' and 'contact_third_party' (and 'financial_action' if funded; 'publish_report' for release) from a named human, plus independent ethics-review clearance. No approval exists as of this finding.
findings.note: Design only; see specific.consultation_design. Approval keys to be computed from the exact design detail dict at request time.

findings.claim: Q3: Sampling design proposal - stratified two-stage probability sample (7 provinces x urban/rural municipality type; PSUs = wards from NPHC 2021 frame, PPS; households by systematic listing; one adult per household by Kish or random selection), with purposive oversamples of project-affected communities analysed separately and never pooled into national estimates without design weights.
findings.note: Method choice; sample sizes to be set by power calculation after retrieving NLSS IV design effects (14A) - no sizes stated in r1.

findings.claim: Q3: Group identity, disability status and caste/ethnicity are collected only with explicit, separate consent, using official NPHC 2021 categories and the Washington Group Short Set; results are reported only where cell sizes and SEs meet a pre-registered suppression rule, with no ranking of groups.

data_gaps: Official gazetted text of Environment Protection Rules 2077 not yet located on lawcommission.gov.np (only secondary copies found).
LARR Policy 2015, Forest Act 2076, Individual Privacy Act 2075, Statistics Act 2079, Disability Act 2074 and RTI Act 2064: exact official URLs not located.
ILO C169 ratification record and CEACR comments for Nepal not retrieved.
No known comprehensive register of project-induced displacement in Nepal; evidence is project-by-project and skewed to MDB-financed projects.
Resettlement outcome evaluations (ADB IED, WB IEG, KfW) not retrieved; project titles and years unverified.
Survey design parameters (sample size, design effects) await 14A NLSS IV design documentation.
Legal preconditions for conducting a survey in Nepal (Statistics Act, ethics body jurisdiction) unverified.

assumptions.text: MDB frameworks are recorded as requirements only for projects they finance; they are not treated as Nepali law.
Project-affected-household evidence from complainants, NHRC and academic sources is kept as separate values from project self-reporting; differences are explained, not reconciled.
Consultation survey is design-only; its outputs are hypothetical until approvals and ethics clearance are recorded.
Group classifications use NPHC 2021 official categories and the legal schedule of indigenous nationalities; no ranking or characterisation of groups.

challenges.text: Land Acquisition Act 2034 is also in your lead set; please share one observation set for the Act text and confirm the legal status of the 2015 LARR policy so 14C and 11A do not extract divergent readings.

Please add land acquisition/compensation disputes, local obstruction and court injunctions as coded delay causes in the DeliveryConstraints panel; 14C will supply project-level safeguard categories. Faster delivery must not be modelled by assuming weaker safeguards without reporting the welfare trade-off.

Disaster-induced relocation and project-induced displacement should be recorded separately; please flag hazard-exposed project sites (e.g. GLOF-exposed hydropower) so resettlement-site risk can be assessed.

Source-tier questions: NHRC Nepal, KfW evaluations and accountability-mechanism findings are not in the catalog (or fall under generic tiers); request tier assignment. Watch item: project self-reported resettlement figures vs complaint/inspection findings - expected methodological differences, not errors.

Any strategy (STR-A..E) that accelerates large hydropower/road/airport investment should be audited for whether displacement and FPIC costs, timelines and legal risk are included; 14C evidence is pending.

uncertainty: Total for r1: nothing retrieved. Key uncertainties: (1) legal texts, amendment status and binding force of the LARR policy are unverified; (2) Nepal's C169 ratification and any domestic FPIC procedure must be confirmed from NORMLEX and Nepali law; (3) displacement evidence is fragmentary and biased toward MDB-financed projects, so no national total can be estimated; (4) many URLs are from general knowledge and unverified (marked in leads); (5) the survey design is hypothetical and its feasibility depends on legal preconditions and human approvals that do not exist.

safeguard_requirements.method: Build a requirement matrix row per obligation (screening, consultation, disclosure, consent/FPIC, compensation basis, non-titled occupants, livelihood restoration, grievance, monitoring) x column per instrument (Nepal Constitution; EPA 2076/EPR 2077; Land Acquisition Act 2034; LARR Policy 2015; Forest Act 2076; RTI Act 2064; Disability Act 2074; ILO C169; UNDRIP; WB ESF; ADB SPS 2009/ESF; AIIB ESF; IFC PS). Each cell = verbatim provision + article/rule number + observation id of the retrieved text. Then a gap matrix: where MDB standards exceed Nepali law (to be determined from texts, not presumed).

instruments.note: Official gazetted text still to locate on lawcommission.gov.np; ECOLEX/DPNet are secondary copies.

instruments.instrument: Land Acquisition, Resettlement and Rehabilitation Policy 2071 (2015)
Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2074 (2017)
National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities Act 2058 (2002)
UN treaty-body and Special Rapporteur recommendations on Nepal
World Bank ESF (ESS1, ESS5, ESS7, ESS10) and legacy OP 4.12/4.10

obligation_rows: entitlements of non-titled occupants, tenants, informal users

gap_matrix.note: Populated only after texts are retrieved; no gap is asserted in r1.

open_legal_questions: Is the 2015 LARR policy binding on all public projects or only where adopted in project agreements?
Does any domestic statute or procedure operationalise C169 consultation/consent, or is it applied only through MDB project conditions?
Which tier of government approves EIA/IEE for provincial and local projects after federalisation, and does the consultation duty differ by tier?
How do Supreme Court decisions (e.g. Nijgadh airport) interpret EIA and consultation duties?

displacement_evidence.method: Evidence table, one row per project: sector, financier(s), approval year, safeguard framework applied, affected persons/households (physical vs economic; titled vs non-titled; indigenous/Dalit/female-headed shares where reported), compensation paid vs entitled, time to payment, livelihood-restoration outcome vs baseline, grievances/complaints and resolution, evaluator and independence (self-evaluation vs independent evaluation vs accountability mechanism vs academic/NHRC). Counts are recorded only as published with their definitions; no pooled Nepal-wide displacement total is estimated because no census of project-induced displacement is known (to verify).

known_methodological_issues: Selection bias: evaluations exist mostly for MDB-financed projects; domestically financed projects (majority of roads) may have no public resettlement monitoring.
Self-reported completion data vs independent evaluation vs complainant accounts differ in purpose and should be kept as separate values (CLAUDE.md rule 4).
Definitions of 'affected' differ (land loss threshold, physical vs economic displacement, titled only vs all users).
Compensation in current NPR at different dates must be deflated (GDP deflator/CPI) before comparison; Nepal FY vs calendar year stated per value.
Displacement from disasters (13A) and from projects are distinct; overlap on hazard-exposed sites handled via 14C-L47 overlay.

fielding_gate.rule: No piloting, enumerator recruitment, contact with any person/organisation, online deployment or publication of the instrument without (a) recorded approval by a named human in state/approvals.json for each gated action and (b) documented independent ethics-review clearance. Agents cannot grant approvals (src/orchestrator/approvals.py rejects agent-like approver ids).
gated_actions_required: financial_action (if any payment to enumerators/firms or participant compensation)
legal_prerequisites_to_verify: Statistics Act 2079 provisions on surveys by non-government bodies (14C-L13)
Individual Privacy Act 2075 consent and data-handling duties (14C-L12)
Applicable ethics review body: NHRC for health-related items; otherwise a Nepal-based institutional review board (14C-L41)

objectives: Measure citizens' development priorities across the 12 welfare objectives (src/economic_model/welfare.py) without anchoring on GDP
Measure perceived procedural fairness, access to information and grievance channels for infrastructure
Measure accessibility barriers to participation (disability, language, literacy, distance, gender)
Separately document experiences of project-affected households (oversample, not pooled)

sampling.frame: NPHC 2021 ward-level enumeration (NSO) - access conditions to verify (14C-L45, 14C-L46)
sampling.design: Stratified two-stage: strata = 7 provinces x urban/rural municipality type; PSUs = wards selected PPS; households by systematic sampling from fresh listing; one adult respondent (18+) per household by random selection. Optional booster strata for project-affected areas identified from RP/EIA documents (displacement_evidence) - analysed as a separate domain.
sampling.size: pending - to be set by power calculation using NLSS IV design effects (14A) and minimum detectable differences by province and sex; no size fixed in r1
sampling.weights: Design weights x non-response adjustment; post-stratification to NPHC 2021 margins (province x sex x age group); report design-based SEs.
sampling.migrant_households: Absent members recorded via proxy module; absent migrants not interviewed without separate approval.

modules: priorities ranking across welfare objectives (randomised order)
experience of land acquisition or displacement (screened)
optional identity items (caste/ethnicity, mother tongue) with separate consent
instrument.languages: Nepali plus major mother tongues by stratum per NPHC 2021 language data; forward-back translation and cognitive testing (cognitive testing itself is fieldwork and gated).
instrument.item_benchmarking: Reuse validated items from existing Nepal surveys where licences permit (14C-L44).

consent.process: Oral or written informed consent in the respondent's language, read aloud; covers purpose, independence (NEPAL 3T is not a government body and cannot promise projects or compensation), voluntariness, right to skip/withdraw, risks, data use and retention, contact for complaints.
consent.special_cases: Separate consent for sensitive modules (displacement, identity, disability); no interviews of minors; guardian/supported decision-making for persons who need it per disability-rights guidance; community-level consent/notification in indigenous areas in line with C169 principles in addition to individual consent.
consent.no_inducement: No promises of benefits; any token compensation requires financial_action approval.

accessibility: Multiple modes (in-person primary; phone only for follow-up with consent)
Audio/pictorial response cards for low literacy
Sign-language interpreter option and accessible venues for group sessions
Female enumerators available for women respondents
Scheduling around agricultural seasons and festivals

data_protection.principles: Data minimisation; pseudonymisation at collection (IDs separated from names); GPS stored only at ward level in analysis files; encryption at rest and in transit; access restricted to named researchers; retention period and destruction plan set before fielding; no raw microdata published; aggregated outputs subject to small-cell suppression rule; compliance with Individual Privacy Act 2075 (to verify).
data_protection.storage_location: pending decision by human data controller (in-country vs external hosting is itself a decision requiring review)

risk_safeguards: Do-no-harm screen for respondents in contested project areas (risk of retaliation); protocol to pause fieldwork
Referral information for grievance/legal aid bodies (verify before use)
Enumerator training on neutrality; no political party questions and no ranking of leaders or parties
Pre-registration of analysis plan to prevent selective reporting

ethics_review.note: Submission is itself a third-party contact and requires contact_third_party approval.

consultation_design.outputs_if_approved: Province x sex x urban/rural priority distributions with SEs feeding 14B dashboard rows for rights_accountability; separate affected-household domain report.
